title: Why Pla i Llevant tastes the way it does

lede.text: Sun and a salty sea wind shape these island wines. They give concentrated aromas, high alcohol and an integrated acidity that brings structure and vigour.

chapters.title: Island vines near sea level
paras: The vineyards lie on the island of Mallorca, in 19 municipalities, among them Felanitx and Manacor. The vines sit practically at sea level.
Only land the Consejo Regulador has rated fit for the listed grapes counts. The Consejo Regulador is the body that runs the DO. Every bottle is filled inside the zone.

fly.label: Pla i Llevant, Mallorca
fly.caption: Island vineyards, practically at sea level, across 19 municipalities of Mallorca.

chapters.title: A salty wind and a lot of sun
paras: The Embat wind brings freshness, humidity and salt. Growers use green pruning to leave the fruit open to it. The wind also brings a lot of salt.
The strong sun favours phenolic compounds. Reds have medium-high colour. Whites stay light in tone.

chapters.title: Limy soils for aroma
paras: The soils are limy (calizos). They boost the presence of aromatic compounds in the wine.

chapters.title: Grapes, liqueur wines and bubbles
paras: Nineteen grape varieties are allowed, from Callet and Manto Negro to Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.
Yields are capped at 11,000 kg of grapes per hectare.
Liqueur wines are strong, with at least 15% alcohol. White ones smell of flowers and fruit in syrup. Red ones smell of jam, raisins and nuts.
Sparkling wines have tiny bubbles that rise in long chains. They smell of ageing on the lees.
Vino de aguja is the lightly sparkling style. It is fresh and fruity, with aromas from its second fermentation.
